transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just can't really sit still. Like, when I'm in the radiology suite or in class... if I have to stay in one spot, I feel like I'm crawling out of my skin. 

I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but... I can't. I always just end up pacing, or shifting around in my chair, or finding some excuse to get up and move. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, or have you started any new ones in the months since this restlessness began?
No. Um... I'm not taking anything. No prescriptions.
Looking back at your childhood, would you say you were often described as restless or unable to stay in your seat?

Yeah... um, I guess so. My parents actually still bring it up sometimes. Like, from elementary school conferences. 

They said the teachers would always complain that I was out of my seat, or... calling out, rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. So... yeah. It's not just something that started with my radiology training. It was happening way before middle school.
